title: Sunday · Beverly Beach
logline: Wood and the dog on Beverly Beach. The sand dollar. It goes on the sill. It stays there.

panels.composition: Tier 1: Beverly Beach in May, wide, wet-on-wet, the creek cutting the sand to the surf, the headland, the light doing what it does for twenty minutes. A man carrying a dog.

image.prompt: a wide wet-on-wet watercolor of a Pacific Northwest beach in May with a creek cutting across the sand to the surf, a headland, a brief sunbreak, a small man carrying a dog, no words

panels.name: Beverly

panels.composition: Tier 2: the man setting the dog down at the tide line; the dog, thirteen and a half, walking four steps, sitting. Beside the dog, in the wet sand: a sand dollar, whole.

image.prompt: a man setting an old dog down on wet sand at the tide line, the dog sitting, and beside it a whole sand dollar half-buried, watercolor

panels.name: Whole

panels.composition: Tier 3: the sand dollar in his hand. Whole. A thing that is almost never whole.

image.prompt: close-up of a weathered hand holding a whole unbroken sand dollar, clean ink over a pale wash

panels.name: In hand

panels.composition: Tier 4: the garage sill. Three jars now: brushes, nibs, and the third with the sand dollar in it. The rain on the window. The dog asleep below. The sill is complete.

image.prompt: a small casement window sill in a garage studio with three jars: brushes, pen nibs, and a single sand dollar in the third, rain on the glass, an old dog asleep beneath, watercolor, no words
image.notes: The sill's third jar arrives. The Empty Chair's sill is complete from here.

panels.name: The sill

art.line: razor-sharp, confident brush and ink; pristine perspective; crisp silhouettes; zero crosshatch in close-ups
art.palette: dailies: black ink, one spot tone at most. Sundays: wet-on-wet — gray-green moss, fog, rusted tin, bruised dusk
art.paper: bristol for dailies; 140 lb Arches cold-press for Sundays

notes: The sand dollar. The third jar. The sill is ready for 2014.
